title: Notable recent papers: biology and biomedicine arXiv — 2026-11-03
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. Attention evidence for this just-announced batch is sparse, so this is an inferred relevance ranking rather than a popularity ranking. arXiv covers only part of biomedical research; much experimental and clinical preprint work appears on bioRxiv or medRxiv.

sections.title: Headline
sections.text: Today's latest arXiv biology and biomedicine announcement batch contains 12 selected papers from 48 unique candidates. The strongest patterns are peptide and protein property prediction, cancer and variant genomics, and single-cell or multimodal biological data methods. The agenda is to compare each claim with its reported evidence and identify what's still untested. arXiv has no official trending chart, attention evidence is sparse, and its biomedical coverage is incomplete; this is an inferred relevance ranking, not a popularity ranking.

sections.title: PeptSol: A Translational Benchmark for Protected-Peptide Solubility in Drug Manufacturing
sections.abstract: PeptSol benchmarks prediction of protected-peptide solubility relevant to liquid-phase peptide synthesis, using 1,388 curated measurements and chemistry-aware train/test splits.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report a best macro-F1 of 0.843 for binary solubility in the historical subset, but no foundation model consistently beats a fingerprint-plus-descriptor baseline across tasks and splits.
sections.unique_caveat: The 1,388 records cover 84 parent sequences and 101 protected structures, with 92.5% from one historical programme. Retrospective solubility prediction does not establish coupling yield, recovery, or process performance.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct peptide-manufacturing relevance; arXiv says accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 AI for Drug Discovery workshop; compares seven molecular encoders on a source-curated benchmark.

sections.title: Evolutionary characterization of whole-genome doubling across human cancers
sections.abstract: The authors integrate genomic, evolutionary-timing, and multi-omic analyses to characterize whole-genome doubling across 41,332 tumours from 12 cancer types.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that driver mutations often precede WGD and that post-WGD chromosome-arm losses are less cancer-type-dependent; WGD-positive tumours also show reduced interferon and HLA-presentation programmes linked to epigenetic remodelling.
sections.unique_caveat: These are analyses of tumour datasets and associations, not intervention-based proof that WGD causes the reported immune changes or clinical outcomes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Large multi-cancer genomic analysis with explicit timing and multi-omic evidence; directly in genomics and population/evolution categories.

sections.title: RangeFinder: Predicting Ligand Property Ranges from Protein Pockets
sections.abstract: RangeFinder predicts ranges for nine ligand physicochemical properties from protein-pocket structure, chemistry, and evolutionary context to help narrow molecular search.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose pocket-level property-range prediction as a complement to proposing or scoring individual ligands and report 12.2 ms inference per pocket.
sections.unique_caveat: Evaluation is limited to pockets with at least three known ligands; the authors note possible homology overlap across UniProt-based splits. Prospective ligand discovery or binding has not been demonstrated.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct protein–ligand relevance and q-bio.BM cross-list; arXiv says accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 AI for Drug Discovery workshop; BioLiP2 evaluation reports range-IoU 0.464 ± 0.002 and Reduction-Recall F-score 0.543 ± 0.011 against deployable baselines.

sections.title: An auditable agentic pipeline for variant-to-gene prioritisation, validated against orthogonal functional evidence
sections.abstract: V2G records evidence retrieval and ranks candidate genes for GWAS loci; the authors test whether a language model's reranking gains actually depend on the retrieved evidence.
sections.claimed_contribution: On 135 loci with successful retrieval, model reranking improves Precision@1 over the evidence ordering, but the authors find no detected difference from Open Targets L2G or training-membership baselines; their controls indicate the gain reflects recall of known genes more than use of the presented evidence.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper reports train/test overlap and retrieval-conditioned subsets; an auditable evidence trail is not proof that an agent reasoned from that evidence.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct variant-to-gene genomics task; frozen benchmark and reproduction code are reported; the abstract quantifies results on held-out loci and explicitly tests evidence-row shuffling and known-gene recall.

sections.title: Coupling cellular trajectories and RNA kinetics on continuous expression manifolds with ManifoldVelo
sections.abstract: ManifoldVelo jointly fits pseudotime, continuous spliced/unspliced RNA trajectories, and kinetic dynamics, with tests on simulated cyclic and branching processes and real single-cell datasets.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report improved pseudotime and velocity comparisons on selected benchmarks and transfer of temporal and velocity predictions to new cells using spliced RNA with a fixed reference.
sections.unique_caveat: Inferred pseudotime and RNA velocity are computational estimates; agreement with marker or stage patterns is not direct time-resolved validation of every cell's trajectory.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct RNA/transcriptomics relevance; comparisons span cyclic and branching simulations plus real-data analyses; arXiv comment links code and numerical source tables.

sections.title: Automatic Generation of Novel Highly-Functional Molecular Sequences
sections.abstract: The authors compare sequence-generation strategies on two complete fitness landscapes and report that a training-free information-theoretic method finds rare high-fitness sequences more effectively than the tested variational autoencoders.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors claim a faster, training-free information-theoretic search can outperform tested ML/AI generation methods at finding rare high-fitness sequences; antimicrobial peptide selectivity is discussed as an application, not demonstrated as a wet-lab result here.
sections.unique_caveat: The second landscape is digital life, and the paper does not report synthesis or antimicrobial/cytotoxicity assays of generated peptides.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct biomolecular sequence-design fit; tests against two complete landscapes, including an experimentally assayed DHFR landscape; first-listed in the focused biomolecules category.

sections.title: The DynaCell Evaluation Suite for Dynamic 3D Virtual Staining of Live Cells
sections.abstract: DynaCell provides paired 3D live-cell imaging data, baseline virtual-staining models, and multi-level metrics to compare image fidelity, organelle segmentation, and cell-phenotype similarity over time.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors find regression baselines better localize organelles while a generative baseline better captures phenotype distributions, showing that one metric can hide different model strengths.
sections.unique_caveat: Benchmark results do not validate virtual staining as a replacement for fluorescence in biological experiments; temporal consistency and broader paired data remain important follow-up areas.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in quantitative biology; arXiv says accepted to the NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations and Datasets Track; benchmark spans three cell types, two microscopes, four organelles, and three perturbation states, and releases data/code/checkpoints.

sections.title: HistoTx: Early fusion of H&E images and spatial transcriptomics at varying spatial transcriptomics resolution with self-supervised learning
sections.abstract: HistoTx fuses histology-image and spatial-transcriptomic tokens in a shared transformer and evaluates image-only and multimodal inference across gene-expression and pathology tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report stronger gene-expression prediction than image-only baselines on several benchmarks and additional gains when transcript data are provided at inference.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors also report drops on some image-only cancer-subtype classification tasks; benchmark gains do not establish clinical utility or robust transfer to new institutions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in genomics and quantitative biology; arXiv says presented at the ICML 2026 multimodal life-sciences workshop; evaluated on spatial-transcriptomics and pathology benchmarks.

sections.title: Can agents reliably design therapeutic antibodies?
sections.abstract: The authors evaluate agentic antibody design under instruction-following and black-box optimization settings, finding trade-offs among tool use, design history, exploration, and optimization.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that tools improve instruction following and sequence exploration but reduce optimization performance, while design history improves optimization at the cost of exploration.
sections.unique_caveat: All reported optimization is in silico; the paper does not establish experimental binding affinity or therapeutic activity of newly designed antibodies.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct antibody-design focus and q-bio.QM cross-list; tests ten expert-validated affinity-improvement tasks and compares its in-silico optimizer with Bayesian optimization.

sections.title: Canonic hemoglobin-oxygen equilibrium: Reassessing the role of cooperativity
sections.abstract: The authors reformulate hemoglobin–oxygen equilibrium in a canonical model of the red-cell environment and predict lower cooperative interaction energies than grand-canonical treatments.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors argue that a canonical red-cell model predicts smaller oxygen-binding fluctuations and that large cooperative energies can produce unstable oxygen release within that model.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a theoretical reformulation; the abstract does not report new red-cell experiments testing the predicted oxygen hopping or instability.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in biomolecules and biological physics; arXiv lists a Journal of Chemical Physics reference and DOI; the paper directly revisits a classic biochemical binding model.

sections.title: Attribution-based diagnostics for single-cell foundation models
sections.abstract: The authors use post-hoc attribution to inspect whether single-cell RNA foundation models rely on biologically meaningful features across cell annotation and perturbation-prediction tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that attribution can expose feature use and model behavior missed by predictive metrics alone, while showing that interpretation depends on the chosen reference, baseline, and null model.
sections.unique_caveat: The perturbation analysis uses a controlled synthetic setting; attribution patterns are not themselves proof of causal gene regulation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct single-cell RNA focus and q-bio.QM cross-list; tests Cell2Sentence and scGPT annotation and scGPT+STATE perturbation prediction, including a synthetic regulatory-ground-truth setting.

sections.title: Findings-aware Language-Image Pretraining for CT Volume Interpretation
sections.abstract: FiLIP uses report-derived abnormal-finding phrases to supervise CT-volume representations and evaluates zero-shot finding classification and radiology report generation.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report improved multi-label zero-shot finding classification over weakly supervised approaches and utility after fine-tuning for report generation.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not state cohort sizes or external-site details; classification and report-generation benchmark performance do not establish clinical benefit.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct medical-imaging focus; arXiv says accepted to WACV 2027; abstract reports in-domain and external-domain evaluations.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.text: Modeling and narrowing molecular search spaces (PeptSol, RangeFinder, Automatic Generation); genomic interpretation and auditing (WGD, V2G); single-cell and multimodal biological evaluation (ManifoldVelo, HistoTx, DynaCell, Attribution-based diagnostics). These papers report complementary methods, not a validated end-to-end discovery or clinical pipeline.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.text: Prospectively test whether PeptSol guidance improves manufacturing yield and recovery; separate V2G evidence use from known-gene recall on independent functional assays; validate molecule-design predictions with synthesis and binding/activity assays; and test cell-dynamics and virtual-staining methods on independent time courses, donors, cell types, and microscopes.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.text: The batch is notable for peptide and protein-design benchmarks, large-scale cancer genomics, and rigorous scrutiny of AI systems used for biological inference. It is too new for a measured popularity ranking; prospective experiments and external validation remain the clearest next steps.
